items.text: **The grain engine stopped making garbage.** The Air grains made a small new object for every grain (up to 60 a second) and threw it away when the grain ended, and the engine reported in every tenth of a second even when Air was off. An older iPad's sound engine has to stop now and then to clear that rubbish, which can be heard as a regular crackle. Grains now reuse a fixed set of slots and the reports slow down when Air is quiet. They sound the same.

**A second test for the iPad crackle.** Open Battanboo with `?reverb=short` at the end of its address and every reverb is held to 2 seconds, which takes most of the steady work off an older iPad's sound engine. Without it, nothing changes.

**A test for the Bluetooth crackle.** Open Battanboo with `?buffer=steady` at the end of its address and the sound runs on bigger buffers: a little more delay to a touch, more room for a speaker link that hiccups. A note at the top says what the browser gave. Without it, nothing changes.

**No crackle with the binaural beat on speakers.** The binaural tones were added after the limiter, so with a loud score they could push the sound past full scale, and a speaker system that mixes left and right met the two tones' beat once per pulse (in Tempo mode, once per beat). While the binaural beat is on, the piece now steps down by the tones' level, so the total stays under the ceiling; the "Your piece" modes keep the same room. The binaural beat still needs headphones to be heard as a beat.

**Hold pop-ups are now real menus, like the line-ups.** The Air, Look, Next, Record and Audience pop-ups were a thin strip of bare icons that hung off the side of the bar. Now each is a card above its button, in two columns, with a name beside every icon (Cloud look and Loop grains get a heading each). Nothing about what they do has changed.

**The cube has a third look: the room.** With the field in front, the cube steps wall, floor, room. In the room you sit in the middle, front is up, and sounds can move all the way around you, which is what four or more speakers are for. The room was there before but the cube looked the same as the wall; now it turns orange, shows you as a dot in the middle, a ring around you and four speakers at the corners. Grid in front stays yellow, field green, room orange.

**Scrolling zones in pop-ups no longer slide sideways.** The Index's pin and grip buttons hang 6 px past the card's edge, and a finger could still drag the whole list that far left and right, so the last sections seemed to jiggle. The Index, the Record and Share sheets and the other pop-up lists now hold still sideways.

**Soniscale™ in your words.** The Index entry under Air and Space and the credits now describe it as: a real-time resource engine that decides when individual notes need to be transformed into textures at the same pitch, balancing the player intention, the ear of the listener, and the system capacity.
